# HEARTz: Product Reference

HEARTz is a browser-based sound workspace. Its public introduction and playable samples are at https://heartz.app/. The application is at https://app.heartz.app/ and requires an account.

## Main tools

- **Guided sessions:** Choose and adjust ready-made combinations of tones and sound beds.
- **Frequency Lab:** Set a tone frequency and configure supported binaural or modulation options. A binaural difference uses separate left and right signals; stereo headphones are useful for hearing that effect.
- **Converter:** Import a supported audio file and retune its pitch from an A4 = 440 Hz reference to A4 = 432 Hz. This is a ratio of 432/440, approximately -31.77 cents. The current natural-resample method also changes playback duration; it does not preserve tempo. Download the result as an uncompressed WAV file. Processing time and supported export settings depend on the file, browser and selected options.
- **My library:** Save and reopen supported settings and recipes. It is a library of configurations, not a library of uploaded or generated music files.
- **Studio and Laboratory:** Additional beta tools inside the application.

## Accounts and storage

HEARTz uses Firebase Authentication for email/password and Google account sign-in. Account creation is required to enter the application. Supported saved settings belong to the signed-in account within the current browser. Library data is not yet synchronized across devices; users can use the available backup and import controls to move supported settings. Audio files are processed locally and are not uploaded to the account library.

The audio engine combines Web Audio with local application code, including Rust compiled to WebAssembly where the relevant module uses it. Actual audio sample rates and available features depend on the browser, device and selected operation. HEARTz does not claim to control downstream hardware or Bluetooth processing.
